transcript.text: d/w not cleaning pls help, gritty bits left on glasses n bowls, beko

Gritty bits usually mean food debris is being recirculated rather than washed away. The common causes are a clogged filter, blocked spray-arm holes, or an arm being stopped by a tall item; less commonly it is detergent/programme choice or weak heating/circulation. With it switched off and unplugged, remove the lower basket, twist out the filter and rinse it thoroughly under the tap. Then turn both spray arms by hand and check the small holes for debris; rinse them and gently clear holes with a cocktail stick if needed. Also make sure no tall pan, tray or utensil can stop an arm turning. Was the filter dirty or an arm/jets blocked, or do they all look clear?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
ok did it. filter was rank, full of food n grease. upper spray arm was stiff to turn n a few holes blocked w seeds/limescale, got them clear w a cocktail stick. lower arm spins fine

With the holes cleared, make sure the upper arm now turns freely and is not catching tall items in the top rack. Run a normal or intensive programme rather than a quick cycle, with detergent and a typical load. If it is still leaving grit after that, the next possibilities are a damaged/still-restricted upper arm or weak wash circulation, but there is no reason to assume a failed part yet.
[Helpful to see: image "Check and rinse the spray arm" — The spray arm spins to fire water through small jet holes. Check it spins freely and rinse the jets clear of food/grit. It usually unclips at the centre. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
ok ran a normal prog after and its much better now. upper arm spins ok. there's still a bit of a musty smell tho, any ideas?

Yes — after a filter has held food and grease, a musty smell is most often residue/biofilm left in the filter well, sump area or around the lower door seal. With it switched off and unplugged, remove the filter again, wipe out any debris you can reach in the well with kitchen roll, and wipe the rubber door seal and its lower edge with a damp cloth. Then run the dishwasher empty on its hottest programme using a proper dishwasher cleaner/descaler; do not use washing-up liquid. The improved wash result points to the blocked filter and upper spray arm being the main cleaning fault, rather than a failed pump. If the smell remains after that, or it starts draining slowly, it would be worth checking the drain hose/connection or having the drain system inspected.

candidates: Dirty filter or blocked spray-arm jets (high)
Detergent, programme choice, or poor water heating/circulation (medium)
